fr.elements: Main Residence; Pool Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure; Patio Area
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Pool Area; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from the road in both directions.
• Mark the location of the pool on any posted site map or knox box documentation to alert arriving responders to the water hazard.
• Install a fence or barrier around the pool perimeter if one is not already present, to prevent responders moving quickly through the property from falling in during low-light or high-stress conditions.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access drive to maintain clearance wide enough for a fire apparatus or ambulance to pass without obstruction.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency apparatus to reach the rear of the property.
• Cut back dense vegetation that reduces visibility along walkways connecting the main residence to the detached structure.
• Mark the detached structure with a visible address or unit identifier so responders can orient quickly on arrival.
• Keep a gate or path to the rear of the property unlocked and clearly passable for responders on foot.
• Identify and maintain a flat, firm staging area near the front of the property where an ambulance can park clear of the access drive.
• Trim any overhanging vegetation along the access drive to maintain vertical clearance for taller emergency vehicles.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Trees; Ground Vegetation; Multiple Access Routes; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Brush Area; Open Green Space
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly next to the structure to create open space between the plants and the building.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so their branches do not touch or hang over the roof or walls.
• Remove dead or dry ground vegetation within the immediate area surrounding the structure.
• Clear low-hanging branches from trees near the structure to reduce the path fire can travel from the ground up into the tree canopy.
• Cut back vegetation along the edges of the brush area where it approaches closest to the structure.
• Keep ground vegetation mowed short in the open areas between the brush area and the structure.
• Remove any dead plant material from within the shrub groupings nearest the structure.
• Maintain clear passage on all access routes by trimming back any shrubs or tree branches that narrow the travel path.
